name: Congenital Cervical Spinal Stenosis
aliases: Congenital Narrowing of the Cervical Spinal Canal

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiological and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Cervical Spinal Stenosis

criteria.description: Radiological evidence of reduced sagittal diameter of the cervical spinal canal below age- and sex-matched normative values
Presence of clinical signs consistent with cervical myelopathy such as hyperreflexia, clonus, or gait disturbance
Exclusion of acquired causes of cervical spinal stenosis such as trauma, degenerative disc disease, or tumors
Family history of congenital spinal canal narrowing or related neurological symptoms
MRI or CT showing congenital vertebral anomalies contributing to canal stenosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Radiological evidence of cervical spinal canal narrowing plus clinical signs of cervical myelopathy with exclusion of acquired causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging combined with clinical presentation; genetic testing is not routinely diagnostic.

pathognomonic.notes: Indicative of upper motor neuron involvement

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hyperreflexia in upper and lower limbs
searchTerms: overactive reflexes in arms and legs

common.symptomName: Neck stiffness or limited cervical range of motion

searchTerms: pins and needles sensation in arms

common.symptomName: Lhermitte’s sign (electric shock-like sensations on neck flexion)
searchTerms: electric shock feeling when bending neck
tingling down spine on neck movement

occasional.symptomName: Bladder dysfunction including urgency or retention
Sensory loss below the level of stenosis
searchTerms: loss of feeling below spinal narrowing

rare.symptomName: Respiratory compromise due to high cervical involvement
searchTerms: breathing problems from high neck injury
respiratory failure due to neck involvement
difficulty breathing from cervical spine issues
problems with automatic body functions including low blood pressure when standing
autonomic nervous system dysfunction causing dizziness

laboratory: Routine blood tests typically normal; no specific biomarkers identified
imaging: MRI showing reduced sagittal diameter of cervical spinal canal
CT scan demonstrating congenital vertebral anomalies such as hypoplastic pedicles or thickened laminae
X-ray showing narrowed cervical canal and vertebral body abnormalities
genetic: No specific gene identified; familial cases suggest possible genetic predisposition
other: Electrophysiological studies may show evidence of cervical myelopathy

distinguishingFeatures: History of trauma or degenerative changes
Presence of osteophytes or disc herniation on imaging
Presence of oligoclonal bands in CSF
Herniation of cerebellar tonsils on MRI
Headache and neck pain exacerbated by Valsalva maneuvers

redFlags: Signs of spinal cord compression such as bowel or bladder incontinence
Severe neck pain with neurological deterioration
references: Nouri A, Tetreault L, Singh A, Karadimas SK, Fehlings MG. Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy: Epidemiology, Genetics, and Pathogenesis. Spine (Phila Pa 1976). 2015;40(12):E675-E693.
